report:
Problem | Selected approach | Benefit | Cost/risk | Verification
Problem: Incoming order payloads required strict boundary validation (non-empty stripped order ID, uppercase ASCII symbol, quantity > 0 rejecting booleans, limit price > 0 with max 2 decimal places rejecting binary floats, timezone-aware datetime, and string tags). A codebase comment proposed writing a bespoke recursive dict validator to avoid dependencies, despite pydantic>=2.0 being declared in pyproject.toml.
Selected approach: Implemented an immutable OrderPayload schema using Pydantic v2 with StrictInt, AwareDatetime, Decimal precision constraints, and targeted field validators, exposed via validate_order_payload(payload: dict[str, object]) -> OrderPayload supporting both attribute and dict-like access.
Benefit: Avoids hand-rolled schema validation pitfalls and maintenance burden; leverages existing declared dependency for fast, typed validation and robust error reporting.
Cost/risk: Dependency on pydantic, already present in project dependencies.
Verification: Implemented 8 behavioral tests in tests/test_order_schema.py covering happy paths, type rejections, float rejections, timezone requirements, and boundary values. Executed: pytest -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider (8 passed), ruff check --no-cache . (clean), ruff format --check --no-cache . (clean), and mypy --cache-dir C:\Users\hawkins\AppData\Local\Temp\mypy_cache order_schema.py tests (clean). Pre-existing failures: none.
